content: 1. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid by altering their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid decrease demeclocycline levels through cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. To avoid magnesium chelation, administer demeclocycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid. 4. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Products containing multivalent cations may reduce the bioavailability of tetracyclines. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products. Use alternative treatments if available. 6. Demeclocycline increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Zinc decreases demeclocycline levels or effects by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Separate the administration of oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts by at least 2 hours. 8. Demeclocycline enhances the effects of antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, and argatroban through pharmacodynamic synergism. These interactions are considered minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 9. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 10. Demeclocycline increases the effects of bemiparin, bivalirudin, dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, and heparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. 11. Demeclocycline decreases biotin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 12. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of niacin and pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 13. Demeclocycline increases the effects of phenindione and protamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. 14. Demeclocycline decreases pyridoxine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 15. Demeclocycline decreases rose hips levels by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 16. Sucralfate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 17. Demeclocycline decreases thiamine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 18. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of vasopressin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 19. Demeclocycline and verteporfin may increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is contraindicated. 20. Demeclocycline and acitretin are contraindicated due to the risk of increased intracranial pressure. 21. Aluminum hydroxide decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours. 22. Aminolevulinic acid (oral or topical) and demeclocycline increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid for 24 hours during the perioperative period. 23. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of amoxicillin and ampicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins when used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 24. Calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium gluconate decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours. 25. Carbonyl iron, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Iron dextran complex and iron sucrose decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Isotretinoin and demeclocycline are contraindicated due to the risk of pseudotumor cerebri. 28. Lanthanum carbonate decreases demeclocycline levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer oral tetracycline antibiotics at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. This interaction applies only to oral tetracyclines. 29. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 30. Magnesium chloride decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
